messages.author: bec3b6c763e426c0
messages.subject: Error in SEM Model with a One-Way ANOVA design (Multiple Indicator Variable Coding)
parts:
I am trying to run a SEM model to assesses differences in means. I am using the one-way ANOVA design from Green & Thompson (2012, Ch. 24 in Handbook of SEM). Here is the model:

Here, Satisfaction (Y) is a numeric observed DV and Coping Method is a categorical predictor with 3 levels: X1=No Strategy, X2=Discussion, X3=Exercise. I am using the multiple indicator variable (MIC) approach (Green & Thompson 2012), where all three levels of the predictor are included in the regression equation and the Y intercept is constrained to zero. Note also that the model allows variances and covariances and intercepts for the predictor levels. The authors managed to run this model in MPlus, but when I try to run it in R, I get a "sample covariance matrix is not positive-definite" error. The model runs fine in R when I use OLS regression. 
Below is my lavaan code. Any help would be greatly appreciated. 
Note: I tried constraining some of the estimated parameters, but the model still gives the error. When I remove X3, the model runs, but it should also run with all three levels of the predictors given that I am suppressing the Y intercept. 

###Create the data set:
df <- data.frame("X1" = c(rep(1,times=9), rep(0,times=15)),
                 "X2" = c(rep(0,times=9), rep(1,times=6), rep(0,times=9)),
                 "X3" = c(rep(0,times=15), rep(1,times=9)),
                 "Y" = c(22,22,24,25,27,30,22,23,24,30,26,22,25,26,27,34,30,26,26,27,28,29,40,42)
)

### SEM model
sem.m2b <- '
          ## Structural Model
          Y ~  0*1 +  X1 + X2 +X3  #Y intercept suppressed to zero
         
          ### X Intercepts
          X1 ~ 1
          X2 ~ 1
          X3 ~ 1
          '
fit.lc2 <- sem(sem.m2b, data=df, estimator="ML")

messages.subject: Re: Error in SEM Model with a One-Way ANOVA design (Multiple Indicator Variable Coding)

###Create the data set:
df <- data.frame("X1" = c(rep(1,times=9), rep(0,times=15)),
                 "X2" = c(rep(0,times=9), rep(1,times=6), rep(0,times=9)),
                 "X3" = c(rep(0,times=15), rep(1,times=9)),
                 "Y" = c(22,22,24,25,27,30,22,23,24,30,26,22,25,26,27,34,30,26,26,27,28,29,40,42)
)

This creates a dummy code for each group, rather than for G-1 groups.  That is why the sample covariance matrix is NPD.  X3 = 1 - (X1 + X2), so one dummy is redundant with the other 2.

messages.subject: Re: Error in SEM Model with a One-Way ANOVA design (Multiple Indicator Variable Coding)
parts:
Thanks Terence. Interestingly, I can get the model to run by just adding a couple of cases to X3 such that its variance now differs from the variance of X1:

df2 <- data.frame("X1" = c(rep(1,times=9), rep(0,times=17)),
                  "X2" = c(rep(0,times=9), rep(1,times=6), rep(0,times=11)),
                  "X3" = c(rep(0,times=15), rep(1,times=11)),
                  "Y" = c(22,22,24,25,27,30,22,23,24,30,26,22,25,26,27,34,30,26,26,27,28,29,40,42, 31.33333, 31.33333))

sem.1anova.lc <- '

## Structural Model
          Y ~  0*1 +  X1 + X2 +X3  #Y intercept suppressed to zero
         
          ### X Intercepts
          X1 ~ 1
          X2 ~ 1
          X3 ~ 1
          '
fit.1anova.lc2 <- sem(model=sem.1anova.lc, data=df2, estimator="ML", fixed.x=T)
